title: Confidence
description: How much weight a record can bear, and why. Deliberately separates the numeric uncertainty of a value from the qualitative strength of the evidence behind it: a precisely counted number from a single unverified source is not the same object as a roughly counted number confirmed three ways, and collapsing them into one score hides exactly what a reader needs.

grade.description: A: independently verified against a primary source, method validated in the field. B: single reliable source, human reviewed, method validated. C: automated collection, not yet human verified, or a source of uneven reliability. D: indicative only, published to show the shape of a gap rather than to support a claim.

sourceIndependence.description: Number of mutually independent sources supporting the record. Two feeds from the same publisher count as one.

fieldCalibrated.description: Whether the underlying unit costs were calibrated against ground truth in this country and this cycle.

knownBiases.description: Directional weaknesses the producer of the record is aware of. Stating these is not a disclaimer, it is what distinguishes an estimate from an accusation.

magnitude.description: 'material' means the bias could change the conclusion a reader would draw.

publishable.description: Whether this record may appear in public output. Grade D records are frequently retained for internal analysis and withheld from publication.
